historical_reviews.v3_1: The Wistron rule assigns I3C to BMC/platform management unless a project specification overrides ownership. ED-04 permits conditional execution after the controller, CPU0 target and expected response package is supplied.

original_test_intent: Validate that the platform-management I3C path associated with CPU0 exposes the project-specified controller and target population with correct identities, dynamic/static addresses and safe read responses.
original_method: The platform owner binds CPU0 to the exact BMC/OOB I3C controller, mux or bridge and target devices, provides address-assignment and safe-read rules plus an expected response matrix, then an agent performs bounded discovery and approved reads while monitoring management and CPU health.
manual_activity: The platform engineer identifies CPU0's management-I3C ownership and topology, approves controller access, target/address lifecycle, permitted CCC/private reads, expected values, health limits and recovery; the FAN BD FRU row remains separate.
required_inputs: CPU0 socket/package identity and board revision
BMC/OOB I3C controller, port, bridge and mux topology
CPU0-associated I3C target PID/BCR/DCR and static/dynamic address map
Whether DAA is pre-existing, observable or explicitly allowed to run
Permitted broadcast/direct CCC and private-read allowlist
Vendor I3C tool/API version and BMC firmware compatibility
Expected target presence, address, identity and response matrix
CPU/BMC temperature, power, error and management-health limits
Independent management/console recovery and maintenance approval
safety_requirements: Do not run the Fan Board FRU command as evidence for this row
Do not infer host /sys/bus/i3c ownership; use the approved BMC/OOB path
Do not scan unspecified controllers or address ranges
Do not issue DAA, reset, enable/disable-event, write or other state-changing CCC without separate approval
Do not read undocumented registers or disturb CPU power, reset, telemetry or firmware state
Stop on bus contention/hang, address reassignment, target loss, BMC instability, CPU/thermal/power anomaly or unexpected event
Use secret-safe management access and preserve complete raw output
agent_execution_scope: Verify source key and CPU0-to-controller/target binding
Confirm the vendor interface and existing address state without changing it
After approval, enumerate only the mapped controller and collect approved identity/status reads
Correlate PID/BCR/DCR, address and response with the expected CPU0 matrix
Capture pre/post CPU, BMC, bus and thermal health
Perform no FRU substitution, broad scan, write, reset, power or firmware action
Report evidence without a formal verdict
engineer_actions: Approve CPU0 I3C topology and target inventory
Approve address lifecycle, CCC/private-read allowlist and expected responses
Provide tool compatibility, health limits and recovery
Keep or de-duplicate the separate same-code FAN BD FRU row explicitly

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not applicable. `ipmitool fru print | grep Fan Board` reads the separate FAN BD FRU domain and never proves an I3C controller, CPU0 target, dynamic address or response. It also exposes the password in argv and hides inventory context.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through the approved BMC/OOB vendor I3C interface, select only CPU0's documented controller and collect its mapped target PID/BCR/DCR, assigned address and allowlisted read responses without invoking DAA or changing target state unless separately authorized.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: I3C, CPU0, code 00453, TBD procedure/criteria and two-minute estimates are preserved; no controller, target, address, CCC, register or response is invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES CPU0 I3C TOPOLOGY, TOOL AND RESPONSE PACKAGE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Fingerprint the platform and CPU0 association, snapshot BMC/controller state, use the documented vendor path for bounded target enumeration and safe identity/status reads, compare every target with the approved matrix, then prove addresses and CPU/BMC health stayed stable.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns the explicit I3C/CPU0 identity into a conditional management-bus test while rejecting cross-variant FRU evidence; Master TBD remains unchanged.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Fan Board FRU readability covers neither CPU0 I3C reachability nor target identity. A host sysfs listing also cannot substitute for the project-owned BMC route.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: I3C discovery and CCCs can reassign addresses or disturb shared management targets; even read operations are unsafe without exact ownership and target maps.

project_override_considerations: A supplied platform specification may identify non-BMC ownership, but it must name the controller, access path and evidence boundary. The same-code FAN BD FRU row must remain independently identified by row, variant and hash and cannot share a verdict by code alone.
expected_evidence: Exact source key, variant/hash and explicit separation from row 1842 FAN BD FRU
Board/CPU0 and BMC/controller/bridge/mux identity with vendor-tool versions
Approved target PID/BCR/DCR and static/dynamic address matrix
Complete raw bounded enumeration and allowlisted response output
Per-target expected-versus-observed comparison with missing/extra/duplicate targets
Before/after controller/address state and CPU/BMC temperature, power, error, SEL and health evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Within this Master row, I3C and CPU0 are incomplete but not contradictory. The Fan Board FRU material is derived-review contamination from a distinct same-code source row, so it is rejected without declaring a Master source conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation class is clear under the explicit I3C test set and Wistron ownership rule. Controller/target maps, tool and expected responses are project readiness inputs; once supplied, a bounded non-state-changing collection is definable under ED-04.

review_improvement: Restores the row's I3C identity, prevents the duplicate code from redirecting execution to Fan Board FRU, and makes CPU0 controller/target/address correlation—not generic inventory—the acceptance boundary.
independent_technical_reasoning: A FRU record is static BMC inventory, whereas I3C validation depends on controller ownership, target discovery state and address-bound transactions. The copied Fan Board filter could succeed while the CPU0 I3C segment is absent or misaddressed. Safe automation is therefore conditional on a CPU0-specific PID/BCR/DCR and address oracle plus a non-mutating command contract; it is not a physical-only task or a permanent semantic blocker.
